feel.name: feel itself
feel.child_ability: tells its own touch from another's (Rochat & Hespos 1997)
feel.test: its own move of its body lands where it guessed (closer to the current or not)

reach.name: look
reach.child_ability: learns what to expect of each thing it looks at (Fantz 1964, habituation)
reach.test: it guesses where the current will be

kinds.name: tell things apart
kinds.test: it tells its own move of the body from the current's push

patience.name: patience
patience.test: it guesses a toy's own later move

shift.name: notice the world changed
shift.child_ability: is surprised when the world breaks its expectation (Baillargeon, violation of expectation)

nudge.name: first reach
nudge.child_ability: learns its kicks move a mobile (Rovee-Collier, contingency learning)
nudge.test: it guesses what its own nudge does to a toy

meet.name: meet an other
meet.child_ability: tells perfect self-contingency from imperfect social contingency (Bahrick & Watson)
meet.test: it guesses what someone else's poke does to a toy

turns.name: time its turn
turns.child_ability: times its turn in a proto-conversation: serve and return (Bateson 1975; Trevarthen 1979; Jaffe et al. 2001)
turns.test: it guesses its own move after someone else's on a toy

expect.name: expect a reply
expect.child_ability: expects a caregiver's response: the still-face upset (Tronick et al. 1978)
expect.test: it guesses someone else's reply to its own move on a toy

mirror.name: recognize itself
mirror.test: it guesses what the mirror shows

change.name: change itself
change.child_ability: picks the way it learns by its own track record, and keeps a change only when it works better: adaptive strategy choice (Siegler & Shrager 1984)

speak.name: speak
speak.child_ability: names a thing to an other and gets a response: first referential words and pointing to share (Bates, Camaioni & Volterra 1975)
speak.test: the LLM adopts a suggestion of its

invent.name: invent
invent.child_ability: makes up games with its own rules
